## Page 2 | Minimum saving and city trends

**Trainer-held until requested.** Use the plot if live R is unavailable.

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d9_evidence_html(3))
html_out(d8_pilot())
html_out(d9_evidence_html(4))
```

<p class="caption">E3: pilot OLS; DiD business-clustered; cutoff HC2; matching business-clustered with matches given. E4: one before measure in the supplied city file. Similar observed earlier trends, if obtained, would inform plausibility rather than prove the counterfactual.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page">

## Page 3 | Cutoff and matching checks

**Trainer-held until requested.**

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d9_evidence_html(5))
html_out(d9_evidence_html(6))
```

<p class="caption">E5: score-58 local window and pre-programme age discontinuity. E6: standardised manager age, staff, area and filtration; nearest neighbour with replacement, no caliper. Supplied gaps and reuse do not constitute a full support diagnostic.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page">

## Page 4 | Data quality and economic advice

**Trainer-held until requested.**

```{r, results='asis'}

html_out(d9_evidence_html(8))
```

<p class="caption">E7: synthetic-record completeness is not a real-world fieldwork audit. E8 revisits the RCT-linked 2.44 partial model from Day 3 Session 1. Its cost and later savings are assumptions; the saving rule and a benefit-cost ratio answer different questions.</p>
